scope: Normalized glossary/audit data only; preserved HGL source datasets remain read-only.

source.authority_note: Later explicit authoritative revisions supersede conflicting earlier formulas. This seed follows Parts XLIII-XLV for successor/profile/quality/superinheritance geometry and retains earlier PA/IH/PH/Gamma definitions where not superseded.

entries.label: Developmental causal mode
entries.definition: Marks physiology/anatomy as necessarily developable due to the designated inner condition taken as one causal basis. Compound operands remain causally irreducible rather than decomposing into separate PA routes.

source_refs.section: Part I — PA: developmental causal mode

entries.label: Inheritance / provenance
entries.definition: Carries inheritable logical/state properties forward while preserving the operand as their inheritance source; source identity and nesting depth remain constitutive information.

entries.label: Irreducible phenotype-profile possession
entries.definition: States that the bearer irreducibly possesses the complete HGL phenotype-profile canonically associated with the operand as a whole-profile of that source.

source_refs.section: Part I — PH: irreducible phenotype-profile possession

entries.label: Archstage global meta-phenotype
entries.definition: Stage-level rule-function governing which concrete phenotypic outputs are biologically admissible across the organism. Globality means universal governance, not identical local output.

source_refs.section: The fourth layer: global Archwomanhood/Archmanhood meta-phenotype Γ

entries.label: Stage-relative biological necessity
entries.definition: The proposition holds in every phenotype realization permitted by the current Γ stage-regime; this is stage-biological, not unrestricted metaphysical, necessity.

entries.label: Stage-relative biological possibility
entries.definition: The proposition holds in at least one phenotype realization permitted by the current Γ stage-regime.

entries.label: Unflaw predicate
entries.definition: The physically instantiated feature significantly increases the quality of the whole physical structure/form. UD is globally demanding and is not the logical negation of FD.

source_refs.section: 238. Flaw and Unflaw: exact canonical definitions

entries.label: Flaw predicate
entries.definition: The physically instantiated feature decreases quality in at least one relevant physical extent, region, component, relation or organized part. FD may coexist with UD unless an extra incompatibility axiom is adopted.

source_refs.section: 238. Flaw and Unflaw: exact canonical definitions

entries.label: Superinheritance
entries.definition: Typed source-preserving closure over an entire source axis/domain, retaining each member as a separately indexed inherited source rather than replacing the domain with its terminal state.

source_refs.section: Part XLII — 303. SIH exact canonical definition
305-307. SIH noncollapse, negation scope, axis typing

entries.label: Bounded Superinheritance
entries.definition: Superinherits every state on typed source axis i whose coordinate beta satisfies a <= beta < b, preserving coordinate, polarity, category, dimensional order and source key.

entries.label: Prefix Superinheritance
entries.definition: Historical predecessor closure for a limit coordinate. It excludes the target and all future coordinates, preventing self/future-inheritance contamination.

entries.label: Limit-State Closure Constructor
entries.definition: Constructs first-class female/male limit states from typed predecessor domains rather than a literal infinitary Boolean string, preserving indexed provenance and enabling successor-after-limit recursion.

entries.label: Minor-hypercategory saturation bound
entries.definition: Typed HGL boundary completing a local minor-hypercategory axis. It is not a largest mathematical ordinal and is not identical to the next category seed.
